scope: Per-unit qualification during this follow-up, not a claim that all measurements used one final executable.

phase_scope.v5: Header, matrix, chunk decode and index implementations unchanged in v6/v7.
phase_scope.v6: Indexed concurrent workload. Subsequent v7 edits affect native framing/mutation and native scan-tail storage; the measured indexed SWMR path is unchanged.
phase_scope.v7: Final production diff: native mutations, scans and maintenance, including actual 1 GiB/4 GiB disk rewrites.

method.toolchain: Rust 1.95.0, release, all features, Linux x86_64
method.builds: Separate baseline/candidate target directories; identical Cargo.lock and benchmark sources; baseline production files unmodified.
method.timing: No builds or tests run concurrently. Five alternating before/after pairs per workload; all retained.
method.single_process: Pinned to one allowed CPU. Named-operation elapsed median; whole-child CPU median and peak RSS median. peak_rss_max_kib also reports maximum across all runs. A minimal C parent uses wait4, avoiding inherited Python RSS floor. Linux block writes are multiplied by 512.
method.concurrent: Eight following readers plus one pinned reader; 16384 checks per reader per mutation epoch; identical reader counts, snapshots and traces asserted by scripts/compare_load.py. Elapsed/CPU/write medians; maximum RSS across runs; unchanged 5% resource gate.
method.storage: Native single-process suite uses /tmp tmpfs. Explicit disk maintenance and concurrent workloads use the workspace overlay filesystem. These are warm local measurements, not cold-storage or terabyte qualification.

limitations: Boundary validation has a real first-mutation cost for lazy/serialized-directory handles without an existing framing proof. At 200000 records, a single lazy tail mark changes from 13.421 microseconds to 88.149822 milliseconds; 20000 ascending lazy marks change from 17.359829 to 98.416463 milliseconds. Ordinary validated opens and subsequent proven boundaries reuse the proof. No input-sized visited set is added.

A cold single segment mark changes from 5.869 to 6.220 microseconds (+5.98%). Header elapsed medians increase 1.96% to 4.91%. These observations are not zero overhead; no universal 5% pass is claimed.
No new cache capacity or workload budget. Fixed 128-byte stack read prefix on mutation combines small header/footer reads (up to 96 more bytes than the header-only route).
std::BTreeMap allocation remains deferred by the owner. The covered allocation-refusal paths do not establish recovery from every allocation, caller codec or OS process kill.
CRC detects accidental corruption, not authenticity. Unsafe mmap callers must still obey the documented file mutation/truncation contract.
superseded_measurements: Initial shared-target-directory comparisons accidentally used identical executables and are INVALID; none enter these results.

Initial matrix, mark and scan regressions were reproduced and fixed before the selected phases. V4 matrix remained about 12% slower; v5 avoids pointless bitmap LRU updates only when the existing cache can hold every page.

V5 tmpfs 1 GiB rewrite median peak RSS was 4048 -> 5324 KiB. V7 avoids rollback-value storage for formats without transaction markers; the same workload is 4048 -> 4064 KiB. The precise allocator-layout cause of the earlier peak was not established.
V6 mark/reopen regressions around 10-12% prompted the v7 fixed stack prefix; selected v7 large marks improve elapsed by 2.86-6.36%.
An obsolete v3 concurrent run was interrupted and is not counted. Earlier measurements against d6bda27 belong to the prior PR head, not this comparison.

validation.initial_failure: The initial final-suite run detected an obsolete direct-call edge in source_audit.rs after header parsing moved to fault_record_entry_prefixed. The guard now requires both caller edges and mutation identity validation; the full suite then passed. Production code and benchmark binaries did not change for this guard update.

reproduction.build: Build baseline 317fc981e5cb78eec26f6820c9e010baf2873bcb and candidate with separate CARGO_TARGET_DIR values; copy the same benchmark examples and their Cargo.toml entries into baseline. cargo build --offline --release -p varlit --all-features --examples. Match binary SHA256 before attributing measurements to these phases.
reproduction.single_process: cc -O2 measure-child.c -o measure-child; invoke measure-child USAGE_JSON ABSOLUTE_EXAMPLE_BINARY followed by command_arguments. Use taskset with one allowed CPU, alternate before/after ordering, retain five pairs. TMPDIR=/tmp for tmpfs or a disk-backed directory for disk maintenance.
reproduction.decode_fixture: Run oom_maintenance_load prepare-decode BYTE_COUNT CHUNK_BYTES FIXTURE once; use that same fixture on both sides and compare its SHA256 to decode_fixtures.
reproduction.concurrent: python3 scripts/load_scalable.py --suite large --only indexed-r8-20g --total-gib SIZE --epoch-mib EPOCH --reader-checks-per-epoch 16384 --read-seconds 1 --data-root DATA --output OUTPUT --binary ABSOLUTE_SCALABLE_BINARY. SIZE/EPOCH are 1/16 and 4/64. Alternate five pairs and compare with scripts/compare_load.py.
